chunk_findings.detail: The new partial-acceptance guard uses order-sensitive list equality (`keep != list(it.globs)`) to decide whether the request “gains nothing,” so a request whose surviving globs are the same set as the current lease but listed in a different order (or with duplicates) is accepted instead of refused. For example, if the live lease holds globs `["a", "b"]`, another live lease holds `c`, and the agent widens to `["b", "a", "c"]`, `_clash_text` returns `keep=["b", "a"]`; `_clash_rule` returns `(["b", "a"], "")`, so `plan_retarget` treats the partial widening as accepted and the caller writes the lease globs, even though the docstring says a request whose surviving globs are exactly the ones already held gains nothing and must stay a refusal. The check should compare sets (or require a strict superset if this is specifically a widening path) rather than raw lists.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases/lifecycle.py:_clash_rule

chunk_findings.detail: The new withheld hint tells the user to “re-run with them once that holder is done”, but in this command `--globs` replaces the entire list, as the adjacent `globs_dropped` hint states. If an item currently has globs `mine.py` and the user runs an update to `mine.py,pkg/gates/x.py` where `pkg/gates/x.py` is withheld, the update succeeds and leaves `mine.py` accepted. The message then says to re-run with `pkg/gates/x.py`. If the user follows that literally and runs `--globs pkg/gates/x.py`, the command will record only `pkg/gates/x.py` and silently drop the existing `mine.py` glob. The hint should tell the user to re-run with the withheld globs plus the globs they want to keep, not just “with them”.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/update_message.py:20

chunk_findings.detail: The new test no longer isolates the event log to the update under test. It reads the entire event log and only checks that some event with kind `lease.waiting` exists anywhere. If the repository state produced by the fixture or `_two_claims` already contains a `lease.waiting` event (for example from a previously queued claim or another operation), and the partial update withholds `docs/x.md` but fails to append a new `lease.waiting` event, the test still passes. The previous version captured `n = len(EventLog(...).read_all())` before the update and asserted that the post-update delta was exactly `["lease.waiting"]`; removing that delta check makes the test falsely pass when the required wait event was not produced by the update.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_update_globs_lease.py:169

chunk_findings.detail: In the partial-widening success path, `_waiting(log, cfg, it, lease, withheld, queue)` and `L.retarget(log, it.id, lease, accepted, resources)` both receive the same `lease` returned by `plan_retarget`. A partial widening into “another live lease” necessarily involves two distinct leases: the item’s own lease, which should be retargeted to `accepted`, and the other live lease that currently holds the withheld globs, which is the lease whose release should wake this item. The single `lease` cannot serve both roles; if `lease` is the item’s lease, the wait is attached to the wrong lease and the item is never woken when the real holder frees the withheld globs, and if `lease` is the other holder, `L.retarget` mutates the other lease instead of the item’s lease. This makes the changed partial-widening success path incorrect for any partial overlap with a distinct live lease.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/items/_edit.py:421

chunk_findings.detail: The test expects the update to add the new non-overlapping glob `src/c.py` to `st.items["T1"].globs` and `st.items["T1"].lease.globs` while also recording `lease.waiting` for `docs/x.md` under `T1`. That is a hold-and-wait state: `T1` acquires a new hold on `src/c.py` and waits for `docs/x.md`. The previous version of this test asserted exactly the opposite behavior for a widening into a live lease: the edit/lease change recorded nothing and only a `lease.waiting` event was emitted, explicitly citing `DX-no-hold-and-wait`. The new expectation codifies a deadlock-prone state and contradicts that invariant, so a correct no-hold-and-wait implementation would reject the update rather than pass this test.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_update_globs_lease.py:test_widening_partly_into_another_live_lease_keeps_the_subset

chunk_findings.detail: The signature and all the early returns shown now return a 3-tuple `(Lease | None, str, list[str] | None)`, but the terminal success return after the `if resources:` block is still the old two-element `return lz, ""`. Example input: a live lease for item `M1` is retargeted to `globs=["new.py"]` with `resources=None` and no live clash or queued ahead; the function falls through and returns two values. Any caller that unpacks the new three-element contract, such as `lease, msg, accepted = plan_retarget(...)`, raises `ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 3, got 2)` on the normal successful update path.
